correctness.rationale: The normalization is birational and unramified, with exactly q(q-1)/2 conjugate-branch ordinary nodes (verified both from coordinates and original 2011 theorem). Degree-zero Picard gluing on P1 yields a product of norm-one tori; the G action on gluing ratios is signed permutation. A nonsplit-torus normalizer gives a dihedral stabilizer with branch-swap sign, hence integral coinvariants Z/2 and scheme-theoretic fixed group D(Z/2)=mu_2, including infinitesimal characteristic two. For q=5 the stabilizer is S3xS2 with epsilon=sgn3 and Pieri gives 6+4 irreducibles. The exact checker enumerates q=2,3,5 group actions, but general proof does not depend on extrapolating finite tests.

value.rationale: The full projective-symmetry fixed subgroup is a natural complete invariant of a widely studied rational nodal curve, and its uniform group-scheme value mu_2 contrasts with the growing arithmetic genus and detects an infinitesimal fixed subgroup in characteristic two invisible to rational-point counts. The ten-node sextic has a motivated exact rank-10 integral symmetry module with a 6+4 decomposition tied to the same curve used as a branch divisor in supersingular surface geometry. The claim is more than a zeta recomputation or automatic base substitution.
